unit.title: Yesterday and tomorrow
unit.blurb: Take what you do now and say it about yesterday or tomorrow
unit.intro: Same drill, new change: the time. Start from what you do now and move it. For yesterday, use the perfect tense and put _herī_ first: _Pānem edō_ becomes _Herī pānem ēdī_. For tomorrow, use the future tense and put _crās_ first: _Crās pānem edam_. The stem often changes in the perfect (_edō_ / _ēdī_, _legō_ / _lēgī_), so learn the verbs in pairs. Press **Run the drill** when you have met most of them.

roles.o: it is the object (the thing acted on), so it stays accusative

changes.label: Say it about yesterday
changes.explain: For something finished, use the perfect tense: _{v}_ is {v.label} of _{v.lemma}_ (“{v.full}”). _herī_ means “yesterday”. _{o}_ stays accusative, the object.

foilsExtra.why: _crās_ means “tomorrow”, but _{v}_ is in the perfect tense (it already happened). For yesterday: _herī_.

changes.label: Say it about tomorrow
changes.explain: For something still to come, use the future tense: _{v}_ is {v.label} of _{v.lemma}_ (“{v.full}”). _crās_ means “tomorrow”. _{o}_ stays accusative, the object.

foilsExtra.why: _herī_ means “yesterday”, but _{v}_ is in the future tense (it has not happened yet). For tomorrow: _crās_.
